source.note: Compared with the published D&D Beyond chapter on 2026-10-06: https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/au/chapter-1-character-options.

summary: A wizard specializing in life energy and undead servants.

feature.name: Necromancy Spellbook: Familiar
feature.summary: Find Familiar is added to your spellbook. It can use a Skeleton or Zombie form, or a normal form with the Undead type. You may trade one Attack-action attack for your familiar to attack with its Reaction.
feature.text: Find Familiar is always prepared for you. Your familiar can take a Skeleton or Zombie form, or a usual form that counts as Undead. When you take the Attack action you can give up one attack to have your familiar make one attack with its Reaction. (The book adds the spell to your spellbook; the game keeps it prepared.)

feature.name: Undead Vitality
feature.summary: After casting a Necromancy spell with a slot, one visible Undead within 60 feet may heal the slot level + your Wizard level.
feature.text: After you cast a Necromancy spell with a spell slot, one Undead you can see within 60 feet (in the game, the most hurt of your allied Undead) regains Hit Points equal to the slot's level + your Wizard level.

feature.name: Grave Power
feature.summary: While holding your spellbook, Arcane Recovery reduces your Exhaustion by 1, and damage from Wizard spells and features ignores Necrotic Resistance.
feature.text: While you carry your spellbook, Arcane Recovery also removes one level of Exhaustion, and damage from your Wizard spells and features ignores Resistance to Necrotic damage.

feature.name: Undead Thralls
feature.summary: Animate Dead can be cast without a slot once per Long Rest, and any casting may have its effective level increased by 1. Holding your spellbook, your Necromancy-created or summoned Undead gain current and maximum HP equal to Intelligence modifier + half Wizard level (round down); controlled Undead within 60 feet add Intelligence modifier Necrotic damage (minimum 1) on attack-roll hits.
feature.text: You can cast Animate Dead without a spell slot once per Long Rest (the game's Animate Dead is cast before a fight and raises one Undead, so its extra level doesn't add more). Undead you create or summon with Necromancy gain Hit Points (and maximum) equal to your Intelligence modifier + half your Wizard level, and while within 60 feet of you, Undead you control add your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1) Necrotic damage to their attack hits.

feature.name: Harvest Undead
feature.summary: Reaction after damage leaves you Bloodied but above 0 HP: reduce a visible Undead you control to 0 HP to heal yourself for your Wizard level.
feature.text: When damage leaves you Bloodied but above 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to drop an Undead you control and can see to 0 Hit Points and regain Hit Points equal to your Wizard level.

feature.name: Death’s Master
feature.summary: While holding your spellbook: once per Long Rest, a Bonus Action grants Wizard level Temporary Hit Points to any number of your Necromancy-created or summoned Undead within 60 feet. When a visible Undead drops to 0 HP, you may explode it: roll d6s equal to half its unused Hit Dice (round up, minimum 1d6). Creatures in its 10-foot Emanation make Dexterity saves against your spell DC, taking that much Necrotic and losing Reactions until their next turn starts on failure, or half damage only on success. Exploding an Undead you do not control also costs a Reaction and a level 5+ spell slot.
feature.text: Once per Long Rest, as a Bonus Action, Undead you created or summoned within 60 feet each gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Wizard level. When an Undead you can see drops to 0 Hit Points, you can make it explode: creatures in a 10-foot Emanation around it make a Dexterity save against your spell save DC, taking Necrotic damage (d6s equal to half its Hit Dice, at least 1d6) and losing their Reactions until their next turn starts on a failure, or half damage on a success. Your own Undead explode on their own unless you turn it Off in the class tab; another's Undead also costs your Reaction and a level 5+ slot, and only on Automatic.
feature.policy_cost: Your own Undead when they fall

feature.name: Death’s Master: others’ Undead
feature.summary: Explode an Undead you don't control when it drops, for your Reaction and a level 5+ slot.
feature.text: Death's Master can also explode an Undead you don't control when it drops to 0 Hit Points, costing your Reaction and a level 5 or higher spell slot. In a fight it's off until you set it to Automatic in the class tab.
feature.policy_cost: Your Reaction and a level 5+ spell slot
